segments.arabic: [251] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال : حدثنا زهير عن أبي إسحاق قال : حدثني سليمان بن صرد قال : حدثني جبير بن مطعم قال :
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Zuhayr related to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: Sulayman ibn Surad related to me. He said: Jubayr ibn Mut‘im related to me. He said:

segments.arabic: قال رسول الله ﷺ : أما أنا فأفيض على رأسي ثلاثا وأشار بيديه كلتيهما
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “As for me, I pour over my head three times.” And he gestured with both his hands.

notes: Both singular reporting verbs in the chain remain distinct from the two plural verbs. The gesture with both hands remains outside the direct quotation.
The selected wording does not separately name water after the pouring verb; the working English preserves that ellipsis. No handful count is imported from 253.

segments.arabic: [252] حدثنا محمد بن بشار قال : حدثنا غندر قال : حدثنا شعبة عن مخول بن راشد عن محمد بن علي عن جابر بن عبد الله قال :
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Ghundar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Mukhawwal ibn Rashid, from Muhammad ibn ‘Ali, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يفرغ على رأسه ثلاثا
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pour over his head three times.

notes: The digital and historical chain begins حدثنا محمد بن بشار; the modern print begins حدثني محمد بن بشار. The selected plural is retained, not silently replaced.
The short report remains a separate complete numbered account, including the full chain through Mukhawwal ibn Rashid and Muhammad ibn Ali. It is not expanded from 251 or 253.

segments.arabic: [253] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال : حدثنا معمر بن يحيى بن سام حدثني أبو جعفر قال : قال لي جابر
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Ma‘mar ibn Yahya ibn Sam related to us. Abu Ja‘far related to me. He said: Jabir said to me:

segments.arabic: وأتاني بن عمك يعرض بالحسن بن محمد بن الحنفية قال كيف الغسل من الجنابة فقلت : كان النبي ﷺ يأخذ ثلاثة أكف ويفيضها على رأسه ثم يفيض على سائر جسده ، فقال لي الحسن إني رجل كثير الشعر فقلت : كان النبي ﷺ أكثر منك شعرا
segments.english: “And your cousin came to me”—referring to al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah. “He said: ‘How is washing for janabah performed?’ I said: ‘The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to take three handfuls and pour them over his head, then pour over the rest of his body.’ Al-Hasan said to me: ‘I am a man with a lot of hair.’ I said: ‘The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had more hair than you.’”

notes: The full chain includes Ma‘mar ibn Yahya ibn Sam and the singular Abu Ja‘far reporting verb. The selected initial conjunction and the explanatory identification of the cousin are retained.

The dialogue belongs to Jabir’s account. Three handfuls, the rest of the body, the statement about much hair and the reply are all retained. The cousin is not replaced with a new name outside the source identification.
Both English comparisons supply water in the three-handful clause; the selected Arabic does not explicitly name it there. No modern volume or further washing action is inserted.

segments.arabic: [254] حدثنا موسى قال : حدثنا عبد الواحد عن الأعمش عن سالم بن أبي الجعد عن كريب عن ابن عباس قال : قالت ميمونة
segments.english: Musa related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d, from Kurayb, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: Maymunah said:

segments.arabic: وضعت للنبي ﷺ ماء للغسل فغسل يديه مرتين أو ثلاثا ثم أفرغ على شماله فغسل مذاكيره ثم مسح يده بالأرض ثم مضمض واستنشق وغسل وجهه ويديه ثم أفاض على جسده ثم تحول من مكانه فغسل قدميه
segments.english: I set out water for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to bathe. He washed his hands twice or three times, then poured onto his left hand and washed his private parts. Then he wiped his hand on the ground, then rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose, and washed his face and hands. Then he poured over his body, then moved from his place and washed his feet.

notes: The selected digital chain names Musa alone. Both inspected prints name Musa ibn Ismail. The longer name is documented here and is not inserted into the selected chain.
The uncertainty “twice or three times” and the sequence of all actions are preserved. The hand wiped on the ground remains singular; no towel is borrowed from 256.

The Arabic has الاستنشاق (drawing water into the nose) without a separate blowing-out verb. Both English comparisons add blowing out; that additional action is not inserted into this working rendering. Hands/arms wording remains provisional for independent review.

segments.arabic: [255] حدثنا محمد بن المثنى قال : حدثنا أبو عاصم عن حنظلة عن القاسم عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Abu ‘Asim related to us, from Hanzalah, from al-Qasim, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ إذا اغتسل من الجنابة دعا بشيء نحو الحلاب فأخذ بكفه فبدأ بشق رأسه الأيمن ثم الأيسر ، فقال بهما على رأسه
segments.english: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed for janabah, he asked for something like a hilab. He took some in his palm and began with the right side of his head, then the left, then poured over his head with both hands.

notes: The selected digital and modern Arabic end على رأسه. The historical print adds وسط (middle) there. The working English follows the selected wording and does not add “middle”.

The English comparisons disagree about hilab: Bewley gives a milk-pot, whereas EPUB 1.5.258 treats it as scent. The term hilab is retained without resolving that identification inside the hadith. The chapter heading separately retains its explicit “or scent”.

Ibn Hajar’s Fath al-Bari, book of Ghusl, discussion of this chapter at printed pages 440–442, examines the vessel/scent readings and parallel pouring expressions. This supports the provisional action wording “poured” rather than treating قال here as spoken words. The source is linked as commentary, not independent translation approval.
The historical addition, interpretive disagreement and working English require independent review; neither comparison is used to rewrite the Arabic.

segments.arabic: [256] حدثنا عمر بن حفص بن غياث قال : حدثنا أبي حدثنا الأعمش قال : حدثني سالم عن كريب عن ابن عباس قال : حدثتنا ميمونة قالت
segments.english: ‘Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath related to us. He said: My father related to us. Al-A‘mash related to us. He said: Salim related to me, from Kurayb, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: Maymunah related to us. She said:

segments.arabic: صببت للنبي ﷺ غسلا فأفرغ بيمينه على يساره فغسلهما ثم غسل فرجه ، ثم قال بيده الأرض فمسحها بالتراب ثم غسلها ثم تمضمض واستنشق ثم غسل وجهه وأفاض على رأسه ثم تنحى فغسل قدميه ثم أتي بمنديل فلم ينفض بها
segments.english: I poured out water for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to bathe. He poured with his right hand onto his left and washed them both, then washed his private parts. Then he struck the ground with his hand and wiped it with earth, then washed it. Then he rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose, then washed his face and poured over his head. Then he moved aside and washed his feet. Then a cloth was brought to him, but he did not dry himself with it.

notes: All selected reporting verbs remain, including the singular Salim clause and Maymunah’s feminine “related to us”. The full name Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath remains in the chain.

The hand used on the earth is singular and is washed afterwards. The dual hands earlier in the report stay distinct. The selected account mentions the face and pouring on the head, without importing the arm/body clauses from another narration.

Ibn Hajar’s Fath al-Bari, book of Ghusl, discussion of this chapter at printed page 443, explains قال بيده الأرض as a physical action and the cloth ending as not wiping/drying. The lexical explanation is separate from the source; no legal ruling or additional narration is inserted.

The complete ending with the unused cloth is retained. The two English comparisons support that sense; their plural earth-wiping hands and added blowing-out wording are not substituted for the selected Arabic.

segments.arabic: [257] حدثنا الحميدي قال : حدثنا سفيان قال : حدثنا الأعمش عن سالم بن أبي الجعد عن كريب عن ابن عباس عن ميمونة
segments.english: Al-Humaydi related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d, from Kurayb, from Ibn ‘Abbas, from Maymunah:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ اغتسل من الجنابة فغسل فرجه بيده ثم دلك بها الحائط ثم غسلها ثم توضأ وضوءه للصلاة فلما فرغ من غسله غسل رجليه
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed for janabah. He washed his private parts with his hand, then rubbed the wall with it, then washed it. Then he performed his ablution for prayer. When he had finished his washing, he washed his feet.

notes: The selected chain begins al-Humaydi alone; both inspected prints give Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr al-Humaydi. The selected name remains unchanged, with the fuller printed name recorded only in these notes.

The wall, singular hand, subsequent ablution and final feet-washing remain in their source sequence. No parenthetical earth explanation or definition of janabah from the English comparison is inserted.

segments.arabic: [258] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة أخبرنا أفلح عن القاسم عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us. Aflah informed us, from al-Qasim, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

segments.arabic: كنت أغتسل أنا والنبي ﷺ من إناء واحد تختلف أيدينا فيه
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I used to bathe from one vessel, our hands going into it in turn.

notes: The selected digital chain says أخبرنا before Aflah. Both inspected prints use حدثنا. The working English retains “informed us”, with the printed reporting-verb difference documented.
The alternation of their hands in a single vessel is retained. The preceding unnumbered chapter paragraph is preserved separately in Arabic and is not part of this hadith or its narration.

segments.arabic: [259] حدثنا مسدد قال : حدثنا حماد عن هشام عن أبيه عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ إذا اغتسل من الجنابة غسل يده
segments.english: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bathed for janabah, he washed his hand.

notes: The digital and modern source have singular يده (his hand), while the historical print has يديه (his two hands). Both English comparisons use plural hands and add “first”; the working English retains the selected singular and does not add that sequencing word.
This short account remains separate from the neighbouring full descriptions and does not acquire their additional actions.

segments.arabic: [260] حدثنا أبو الوليد قال : حدثنا شعبة عن أبي بكر ابن حفص عن عروة عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Hafs, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

segments.arabic: كنت أغتسل أنا والنبي ﷺ من إناء واحد من جنابة
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and I used to bathe from one vessel for janabah.

segments.arabic: وعن عبد الرحمن بن القاسم عن أبيه عن عائشة مثله
segments.english: And from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, the same.

notes: The full secondary chain from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, through his father, to Aisha and its “the same” pointer are retained as a separate transmission-note segment.
The pinned EPUB 1.5.263 gives the main body without the secondary chain. Bewley 260 includes an abbreviated closing chain; the complete selected Arabic chain is the basis of the working English.
The exact source spelling ابن in Abu Bakr ibn Hafs is preserved. No repeated report body is invented for the closing “the same” pointer.

segments.arabic: [261] حدثنا أبو الوليد قال : حدثنا شعبة عن عبد الله بن عبد الله بن جبر قال : سمعت أنس بن مالك يقول
segments.english: Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabr, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik saying:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ والمرأة من نسائه يغتسلان من إناء واحد
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and one of his wives used to bathe from one vessel.

segments.arabic: زاد مسلم ووهب عن شعبة من الجنابة
segments.english: Muslim and Wahb added, from Shu‘bah: “For janabah.”

notes: The complete chain through Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Jabr and the direct-hearing clause remain explicit. The unnamed wife remains unnamed.
The separate addition “for janabah” stays attributed to Muslim and Wahb from Shubah. The historical print expands Wahb to Wahb ibn Jarir; the selected digital and modern text retain Wahb alone.
The pinned EPUB 1.5.264 includes the added phrase but abbreviates its attribution to Shubah; Bewley 261 retains Muslim and Wahb. Neither is used to shorten the complete selected closing attribution.
